notes: Background: DocInsight is a mid-market KM SaaS (vertical: professional services knowledge bases). Evaluating embeddings-based semantic search to replace noisy keyword search.
Current stack: Postgres + Elasticsearch for metadata, Pinecone pilot for vectors. Wants tighter latency + lower unit cost for batch + online queries.
Initial ask: validate hosted API for quick POC (embeddings + upsert pipeline), then move to Dedicated if throughput/costs justify reserved capacity.

POC scope: 1) ingest 500k documents -> ~1.2M vectors (multiple fields). 2) nightly batch job: ~2M vectors (full refresh) within 2–4 hour window. 3) online query load target: 150–250 qps peak, p50 latency <50ms for vector lookup+filtering.
Security: must support SSO/SAML, SOC2-aligned controls, audit logs, KMS integrations, and a data residency clause for EU customers (they have EU customers).
Pricing sensitivity: trying to stay under $0.02 per 1k embedding-units equivalent; heavy interest in Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, cache profiles) to reduce monthly unit cost.
Competitor notes: currently comparing hosting on Pinecone vs. self-hosted Weaviate; concern: cost at scale and multi-tenant isolation for client data.
Redwood POC notes: Demo (2026-02-15) was positive — search quality comparable to Pinecone baseline. Team spun up hosted embeddings POC on 2026-02-18 (FF call ff_2026-02-18_1234).

POC findings so far: - Hosted API easy to integrate (fast SDK) - Bulk ingestion via Redwood batching + Optimize reduced token calls by ~22% in test ingestion; - Vector DB integration tested end-to-end using Pinecone + Redwood-hosted embeddings.
Quotes from team: 'Hosted flow was fastest to ship — low friction. If we can hit throughput and price targets, Dedicated makes sense for long-term cost predictability.'
Open technical questions: what Dedicated GPU pool sizing is recommended for 200 qps query load with 1.2M vectors? How does Redwood handle cold-cache latency for large KV caches?
Next POC steps: run nightly full-refresh at scale (2M vectors) on hosted infra, capture end-to-end ingestion time and cost; run sustained query load test (48h) to validate p99 latency and error rate.

Sales notes: AE provided preliminary Dedicated pricing worksheet (drive:/pricing/docinsight_estimate_v1.xlsx) — team expects a firm quote after POC numbers. Legal request sent for data residency language (linked).

Decision criteria (stated by Head of Product): search quality parity OR better than current Pinecone setup, predictable monthly cost within forecast, enterprise controls (SAML, audit logs), ability to schedule/optimize nightly batch windows without affecting peak latency.
